description: Use this when you need an organic swept solid whose cross-section changes along its length — a tapering body, horn, bottle, handle, ring band, fairing, or duct — authored as a variable-section sweep along a spine. Inserts `variableSweep(spine, sections, opts?)` into the .kcad.ts `code` immediately before the last top-level return (an empty `code` starts a new script that returns the sweep). Spine: EITHER `spine_points` ([[x,y,z], ...] in mm, interpolated with spline3d; `spine_closed: true` closes the loop for a ring) OR `spine_binding` (an existing Curve3D / Sketch / Vec3[] variable). Each section: `t` in [0, 1] plus a profile — inline `radius` (circle) or `width` + `height` (rectangle), or `profile_binding` (an existing Sketch); profiles are centred on the spine and turned to face along it. Sections are strictly increasing in t, first t=0, last t=1 (omit t on every section to space them evenly). On a closed spine t=1 is the seam and reuses the t=0 profile. Example: { code, spine_points: [[0,0,0],[0,10,30],[0,0,60]], sections: [{ t: 0, radius: 8 }, { t: 0.5, radius: 10 }, { t: 1, radius: 4 }] }. Returns the modified code, diagnostics from re-evaluating it, and `sweep` { volumeMm3, bbox } measured from the built solid (ok:false when the sweep built nothing). The result is a Shape binding: return it, or chain `.union(...)` etc. via add_feature. Orientation is not exposed by this MCP tool until runtime orientation support is wired. Side-effect-free.

binding_name.description: JS const name for the new Shape binding (default: _sweep_<N>).

code.description: The .kcad.ts source code ("" for a new script).

sections.description: Varying cross-sections along the spine; at least 2 entries, strictly increasing in `t`, first t=0, last t=1.

height.description: Inline rectangular profile height, mm (with width).

profile_binding.description: Existing Sketch variable name for this section (instead of radius / width+height).

width.description: Inline rectangular profile width, mm (with height).

spine_binding.description: Existing variable name for a Curve3D / Sketch / Vec3[] declared earlier in the source. Use this OR spine_points.

spine_closed.description: With spine_points: close the spline into a loop (ring band, loop handle).

spine_points.description: Inline spine: at least 2 [x, y, z] points in mm, interpolated with spline3d. Use this OR spine_binding.
